stories.title: New restrictions kick in as Delhi battles pollution
stories.summary: Authorities in New Delhi stepped up anti-pollution measures on Sunday, including higher parking fees and work-from-home orders, seeking to curb toxic smog in one of the world's most polluted capitals.

stories.title: Warmer seas and shifting pressure systems: The signs that suggest the Mediterranean's climate is 'tropicalizing'
stories.summary: Nowhere in the Iberian Peninsula or the Balearic Islands has a tropical climate—for this to be the case, the average temperature in the coldest month would have to be 18°C (64 degrees Fahrenheit) or higher. The contrast between Spain's winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.

stories.title: Why some trees thrive far from home—and what that means for carbon sinks
stories.summary: In a study spanning 192 sites and four continents, researchers have discovered that conifers planted in the Southern Hemisphere grow up to four times faster and are more drought-resistant than those growing in their native ranges.

stories.title: The Great Barrier Reef's most notorious coral killer may actually be helping it
stories.summary: Crown-of-thorns starfish are notorious for devouring coral reefs, but surprising new research reveals these spiny predators may actually help reefs thrive when their populations are kept in check. Scientists studying Australia's Great Barrier Reef discovered that nearly 75% of observed starfish feeding events left behind living coral tissue, rather than destroying entire colonies. By feeding on fast-growing, dominant corals, the starfish create opportunities for slower-growing species to survive, potentially increasing coral biodiversity.

stories.title: Scientists discover the hidden “muscles” trees use to straighten themselves
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that trees can sense their own shape and straighten their trunks using specialized wood that acts like opposing muscles. This remarkable ability helps trees maintain their posture and could lead to stronger forests, better timber, and more resilient crops.

stories.title: Environmental defenders testify about attacks in Latin America linked to Canadian mining companies
stories.summary: The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights heard testimony Oct. 27 from representatives of six countries alleging harm linked to Canadian mining companies’ operations, including four alleged attacks on environmental defenders. stories.title: Young Canadians focus on mental health at key climate trial
stories.summary: At a landmark Canadian trial focused on the government's obligations to fight climate change, the young plaintiffs suing Ottawa over alleged policy failures have sought to focus attention on their mental health.

stories.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track
stories.summary: Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements Friday at a U.N. biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity's destructive toll on nature.

stories.title: Leaders grapple with finance and harmful subsidies at UN’s COP17 biodiversity conference
stories.summary: YEREVAN, Armenia — Visitors entering the main hallway of the 2026 U.N. biodiversity conference (COP17) encounter a mural of a herd of elephants. stories.title: World Lemur Day: How can we save these primates’ forest homes?
stories.summary: More than 100 known species of lemurs live in Madagascar. These primates with large eyes, a pointed snout, and long bushy tails are found only in the island country, where they usually live in large groups on trees.
